items.expected-result: a `file#section` query returns that exact chunk within the production result window
items.evidence:
Positive: single result -- {"hash":"a987548a...","ranking":1,"sourceFile":"/notes/decisions/2026-outage.md","chunkIndex":0,"totalChunks":1}, evidenceByHash fusionStrength:1, legs:[{fts,rank:1}] -- exactly the chunk named by the anchor, nothing else, within the production limit/floor (no overrides beyond vectorWeight:0).
Negative control: 4 rows returned (every note in the bank), fusionStrength varies per row, response flagged "unranked":true, and the top-ranked row is NOT the decision note but the astrolabe note.
items.observed-result: The file#section anchor resolves to exactly its one intended chunk when the section is real (SqliteMemoryStore.Search.cs's PlanAsync: an anchor whose file+section AND-query matches at least one row in that file is used verbatim). For the negative control (`#no-such-section`), the anchor's own strict file+section lookup matches zero rows, so PlanAsync -- by documented design ('so text that merely looks like file#section is searched as text') -- falls back to an ordinary broad-OR full-text search over the whole bank instead of a hard empty result. That fallback is visibly different and markedly weaker than the positive case (noisy, unranked, wrong top hit vs. clean single ranked exact hit), which is sufficient proof the section value is not a no-op: a broken implementation that ignored the section would have returned the SAME clean single hit for both queries, and it did not.
items.acceptance-reason: Positive case matches the item's stated expected-result exactly (exact chunk, production window, vectorWeight 0 isolates FTS/anchor logic from vector luck). The `#no-such-section` negative control does not come back empty (it falls back to ordinary text search, per PlanAsync's own doc comment) rather than a hard-refuse -- recorded here so this run isn't inherited as 'negative control returns empty' by a future run; the fallback is intentional design, not a defect, and it still discriminates (different, weaker outcome) so the mechanism is proven real rather than accidental.

It rejects precisely the 3 documented shapes and only those -- every near-miss negative control (same leading words but wrong exact prefix, or the exact-body rule violated by leading text or a non-digit remainder) is stored normally, so the filter is discriminating rather than blanket-rejecting. Every rejected write reports Stored=false with the policy name in Reason (ADR-0032-style truthful refusal, no fabricated hash/path). The rejected content is fully retrievable, verbatim, from noise_entries (the noise store), and the CLI summary's count matches the sqlite row count exactly.
items.acceptance-reason: All three shapes reject correctly, all four negative controls prove the filter is not blanket-rejecting, and the rejected content and count are independently confirmed in noise_entries and the CLI summary. Reset: `structural disable`; `threshold set 0.98939822280316`.
items.evidence: Baseline: `enabled: True  shadow: False  structural: False  threshold: 0.98939822280316` (matches ADR-0041's shipped default 0.98939822280316). Refuse R1 '[IMPORTANT: Background process foo completed normally. Command: ls -la' -> isError:true, text starts 'invalid-params: This looks like tool output...'. Refuse R2 '[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE] The batch dispatched earlier has finished.' -> same invalid-params refusal. Warn W1 (stack-frame line 'at MyNamespace.MyClass.MyMethod(String x)') -> no isError, warning='This query contains what looks like log or stack-trace output...', search still ran (fts hit returned). Warn W2 ('warn: something happened during startup') -> same warning text, ran with empty results. Clean C1 ('why did the auth build start failing') -> no isError, no log/tool-output warning (only the embedding-engine-not-configured warning), 2 fts hits returned. Structural off + threshold=0.0, clean query -> no structural warning (byte-identical to off). Structural enabled + threshold=0.0, same clean query -> warning='This query's shape (line layout, punctuation density, token structure) statistically resembles tool output...' (the distinct structural message), no isError. Structural enabled + threshold=1.0, same clean query -> no structural warning (score never reaches 1.0). Structural enabled + threshold=0.0 + refuse-tier query R1 -> still refused with the regex message ('invalid-params: This looks like tool output...'), never downgraded to Warn.
items.observed-result: Both ADR-0040 tiers behave exactly as specified: the two unambiguous machine-output shapes are refused before any store call (invalid-params, no fabricated result), and the two narrow log/stack-trace markers only annotate (search still executes). A clean, ordinary query passes through with no guard warning. ADR-0041's structural detector is off by default (a threshold that every score would satisfy has zero effect while disabled), only ever promotes Clean->Warn when explicitly armed via `queryguard structural enable`, uses its own distinct guidance text, respects its threshold setting, and can never override or replace a regex Refuse.
items.acceptance-reason: Every behavioural claim in both ADRs (refuse tier, warn tier, clean pass-through, structural default-off, structural threshold gating, structural never-refuse/never-override) was independently exercised and matched exactly, including using distinguishable guidance text as proof the structural path actually fired rather than a regex tier.

items.expected-result: Watch a scratch directory (`settings ingest scope add`, `settings watch enable`, memory_watch_add) holding x.md, w.md and y.md, plus node_modules/pkg/index.md and .git/notes.md, each with a term found nowhere else. Wait for three watch_files rows, `chmod 000` node_modules, wait 2 s, then edit y.md so watches.last_change_ts moves past x.md's watch_files.updated_at. Read both values while the server runs, because a stopped WAL bank will not open read-only. Stop the server. Replace one word of x.md with a new term of the same byte length and `touch -t $(date -r <t> +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)` it, where t is between x.md's updated_at and last_change_ts. Rewrite w.md at a different size with a new term, and touch it to before its own updated_at. Restart on the same data root. Within seconds memory_search finds both new terms, watch_files shows new updated_at and size for x.md and w.md, and memory_watch_status reads Healthy. Neither the node_modules term nor the .git term is ever found. Premise: before the restart, updated_at(x.md) <= mtime(x.md) <= last_change_ts. A build without ADR-0121 finds neither new term, because it re-queues only files with mtime > last_change_ts. The 5-minute heal pass (WatchHostedService.HealInterval, event 322 at Debug) is optional: it needs a server left up for over 5 minutes (ADR-0121)
items.command: Fixture: watchdir/{x.md,w.md,y.md,node_modules/pkg/index.md,__pycache__/notes.md} each with a unique term (see note on .git substitution below). settings ingest scope add + settings watch enable + memory_watch_add as above. Confirmed 3 watch_files rows (x.md,w.md,y.md only) via `sqlite3 "file:memory.db?mode=ro" "SELECT path,updated_at,size FROM watch_files"`. `chmod 000 $LANE_ROOT/watchdir/node_modules`; sleep 2; rewrote y.md (bumps watches.last_change_ts). Read (server running): watch_files.updated_at(x.md)=1790526520, watches.last_change_ts=1790526606 (premise 1790526520<=t<=1790526606 to be chosen). Stopped server (kill PID 32692). Rewrote x.md replacing ALPHA9x->ZULU777 (same 46-byte length) and `touch -t 202609271829.20` (t=1790526560, inside [updated_at,last_change_ts]). Rewrote w.md at a different size (46->70 bytes) with new term ZEBRAFOX99 and `touch -t 202609271828.20` (t=1790526500, before w.md's own updated_at 1790526520). Restarted: `ai-raccoon --data-root $LANE_ROOT serve --port 0 --idle-timeout 0` (new port 58261, PID 58571). After ~5s: mcp memory_search {query:ZULU777}, {query:ZEBRAFOX99}, {query:DELTA1q(node_modules term)}, {query:ECHO2p(pycache term)}; mcp memory_watch_status; sqlite3 SELECT on watch_files. `chmod 755 node_modules` afterwards to restore permissions.
items.evidence: Pre-restart sqlite read (server running): watch_files x.md updated_at=1790526520 size=46; watches.last_change_ts=1790526606 (>updated_at(x.md), confirming premise range). x.md mtime set to 1790526560 (between 1790526520 and 1790526606) and w.md mtime set to 1790526500 (before its own updated_at 1790526520) while server stopped. Post-restart: memory_search for ZULU777 -> hit on x.md (fts leg); memory_search for ZEBRAFOX99 -> hit on w.md (fts leg); watch_files after restart: x.md updated_at=1790526650 size=46, w.md updated_at=1790526650 size=70, y.md unchanged (1790526606/61); memory_watch_status -> state "Healthy", lastSync 2026-09-27T16:30:50Z. memory_search for DELTA1q and ECHO2p both returned results:[] both before and after the restart.
items.observed-result: The server re-digested x.md even though its touched mtime (1790526560) never exceeded watches.last_change_ts (1790526606) -- a naive 'mtime > last_change_ts' re-queue rule would have skipped it -- and re-digested w.md even though its touched mtime (1790526500) was set BEFORE w.md's own prior updated_at, which a naive rule would also have skipped or misordered. Both were caught because catch-up compares each file's own content fingerprint, not mtime, matching ADR-0121's decision. watch_files shows new updated_at and correct new size for both files; memory_watch_status reads Healthy; the two denied-name directories were never found by search, at any point.
items.acceptance-reason: One deliberate substitution: the sandbox's git-internals guard unconditionally blocks any shell/python write targeting a path containing '/.git/', even a synthetic non-repository fixture, so '.git/notes.md' was replaced with '__pycache__/notes.md'. Both '.git' and '__pycache__' are plain, equally-weighted entries in the same WatchDenySet.Names hash set (src/AiRaccoon.Core/Ingestion/WatchDenySet.cs: {node_modules, bin, obj, .git, .venv, __pycache__, dist, build, target}), so the substitution exercises the identical deny-by-name mechanism the item is testing, not a different one. All of the item's substantive claims (fingerprint-based catch-up per ADR-0121, Healthy status, deny-set exclusion) were verified directly against the real behaviour, so the substitution does not weaken the verdict: pass.
